haiku-low.q1: After the store commit succeeds (steps 1-4), via the gateway. The ack contains {msg_id, seq}, confirming storage and sequence only, not fan-out.
haiku-low.q2: Sender gets an error and nothing is published. Retry must reuse the same msg_id; the store returns the original seq, inserting nothing.
haiku-low.q3: After 30 s without a heartbeat, the presence key expires. A clean disconnect deletes it immediately.
haiku-low.q4: Gateway requests a push; the Offline Inbox entry stays until the client acks that msg_id.
haiku-low.q5: It is logged and not retried. The Offline Inbox entry is untouched.
haiku-low.q6: Pending entries are read, bodies fetched by msg_id, then sent per conversation in ascending seq. Clients drop duplicate msg_ids.
haiku-low.q7: The outbox row is committed in the same transaction as the message, so the relay still publishes it after a crash.
haiku-low.q8: In the in-memory Presence Registry (user_id to gateway node, 30 s TTL). Expiry after 30 s without heartbeat removes it.
haiku-low.q9: Worker queues it to gateway G, which writes it to the socket. The client's msg_id ack within 5 s confirms receipt.
haiku-low.q10: In the Offline Inbox, written in fan-out step 8a before any delivery attempt. Removed on client ack of msg_id or after 30 days.
haiku-low.q11: The user's pending Offline Inbox entries, then message bodies fetched by msg_id from the Message Store.
haiku-low.q12: Unacked event is redelivered by the bus; another worker repeats the whole recipient list. Inbox puts are idempotent on (user_id, msg_id).

sonnet.q1: After step 4, once the Message Store transaction (message insert + outbox row) commits. The ack carries {msg_id, seq}; it says the message is stored with its seq and an outbox row exists, not that anyone received it.
sonnet.q2: The sender gets an error. No outbox row exists, so nothing is published and no one receives it. The retry must carry the same client-generated msg_id; the store then returns the original seq instead of inserting again.
sonnet.q3: 30 s after the last heartbeat (heartbeat every 10 s resets the 30 s TTL); the key then expires and the user counts as offline.
sonnet.q4: Gateway G requests a push; the Offline Inbox entry stays (not deleted).
sonnet.q5: It is logged and not retried. The Inbox entry is untouched.
sonnet.q6: Per conversation in ascending seq. Duplicates are dropped by the client by msg_id (live messages arriving during reconnect are placed by seq and deduped by msg_id).
sonnet.q7: The message insert and the outbox row are written in one transaction, so if commit succeeded the outbox row exists; the relay publishes it later, so fan-out still happens. The client's retry gets the original ack.
sonnet.q8: In the Presence Registry, an in-memory key-value store mapping user_id to gateway node. The 30 s TTL expires the key after heartbeats stop.
sonnet.q9: The Fan-out Worker looks up presence; if the key is node G, it sends the message to G's delivery queue; G writes it to the recipient's socket and starts a 5 s timer. The client acking the msg_id within 5 s confirms arrival (which deletes the Inbox entry).
sonnet.q10: In the Offline Inbox (per-user pending entries, pointers not bodies). Written by the Fan-out Worker for every recipient before any delivery attempt (step 8a). Removed only when the client acks that msg_id (live or after reconnect), or by expiry after 30 days.
sonnet.q11: It reads the user's pending entries from the Offline Inbox (R2), then fetches the message bodies by msg_id from the Message Store (R3), and sends them per conversation in ascending seq.
sonnet.q12: The event was not acked, so the bus redelivers it and another worker repeats the whole recipient list. Inbox puts are idempotent on (user_id, msg_id) and clients drop duplicate msg_ids.
